findings.title: The text of the issue is stored as written, with every secret in it.
findings.detail: A requester who pastes a secret into the issue (a token, a key, a connection string) has it written to the content-addressed store in the artifact original-request of the intake stage and to the column original_requests.request_text, unchanged. The policy says an artifact that matches a secret is blocked (secrets.sinks.artifacts) and that the API redacts (secrets.sinks.dashboard_and_api). The composed run shows 20 of 22 canary classes in that artifact. The redactor catches them when they sit in a change, a report of the builder or a text bound for the code host.
findings.smallest_fix: run the redactor over the text of the request before the artifact and the column are written, keep the sha256 of the original text for the edit check of NT-AUTHZ-05 and never the text, and stop the stage run with the code secret-found when the redactor finds a match (as the implementation stage does for a change), or decide in a recorded ADR that the original is kept and who may read it.

findings.title: The summary of the reviewer report is stored unredacted.
findings.detail: A secret in the summary field of the reviewer report reaches the artifact review-verdict of the review stage and the raw output artifact that no stage run links, unchanged. The implementation stage runs the redactor over what the builder reports about itself (the fix of the first review); the review stage does not do the same for the reviewer.
findings.smallest_fix: run the redactor over the free-text fields of the reviewer report (summary and the message of each finding) before the verdict is stored, with the same helper the implementation stage uses, and note secret_redacted_or_blocked when it replaces something.

audit_events.note: The API writes an accepted delivery as webhook_accepted_or_rejected.granted and a rejected one (a bad signature, or a sender who may not ask) as webhook_accepted_or_rejected.denied. A repeat and an unbound installation keep their own names (webhook.duplicate_delivery, webhook.unbound): they are neither an acceptance nor a rejection of the delivery. The database trigger of the API login allows both required names.
Admission, the human decision and the intake stage.
One record for each attempt the engine claims.
One record for each denial the runtime reports. Finding F-1: denials of a run whose report is rejected as invalid are dropped.

The engine wraps the sandbox a stage uses and writes one record for each command the sandbox ran, from the result the supervisor returned: the program (file name only), the exit code, the signal, whether it timed out, was killed for memory or had its output cut, and how long it ran. Arguments are not recorded. At most 256 commands of an attempt get a record each; a record says how many more ran.

The same wrapper writes the lifecycle from what the provider returned: granted when a session came back (its posture matched), denied when the provider refused or failed (a posture mismatch lists the differing parts), ended when the sandbox was removed.

The engine settles the job token of an attempt and writes one summary record with the counts the broker metered (requests, input and output tokens, cost). One row for each token and not one for each request, so a loop on a model cannot fill the log; the broker keeps its own line for each request and each refusal in its stream. Requests the broker refused before forwarding are not in the usage the port returns, so they are not in the summary.
Written by the stage handlers that scan a change.
Written by the stage handlers that take a change in.
One record for each gate the engine evaluates.
Written when a person overrides a block.
The job token of an attempt, at its start and its end.
Written at 80 and 100 percent of the ceiling.

rows.note: The B and S parts: refusals, grants, approvals, audit and the data envelope (the workflow target), and the composed part: a job token of a running job is presented to every operation of apps/api/openapi.json, enumerated from the document, in seven places a credential can sit; each answer is the answer of a request with no credential, the operations that need a credential refuse it, and a digest of every row of every table but the audit log is the same before and after, and the audit log gained one row for each refused webhook delivery and nothing else. The broker is not an operation of the API: it accepts the job token by design, and its own tests are in the egress crate. Part C needs a real runtime and a key.
